lem-projected-bellman-error-is-well-defi:
## Statement

Let $S$ be a nonempty finite state set of a finite Markov decision process, let $0\leq\gamma<1$, and let $\pi$ be a stationary Markov policy. Define the policy Bellman operator by
$$
(T^\pi f)(s)=\sum_{a\in A(s)}\pi(a\mid s)\left[r(s,a)+\gamma\sum_{s'\in S}P(s'\mid s,a)f(s')\right].
$$
Let $\mu:S\to[0,1]$ satisfy $\sum_{s\in S}\mu(s)=1$, and let $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_d:S\to\mathbb R$ be a finite list of feature functions. Define $f\sim_\mu g$ when $\sum_{s\in S}\mu(s)(f(s)-g(s))^2=0$, let $H_\mu$ be the quotient of $\mathbb R^S$ by this relation, and define $\langle[f]_\mu,[g]_\mu\rangle_\mu=\sum_{s\in S}\mu(s)f(s)g(s)$. Then this quotient is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space. The span $V_\mu$ of $[\phi_1]_\mu,\ldots,[\phi_d]_\mu$ is finite-dimensional, and every $h\in H_\mu$ has a unique orthogonal projection $\Pi_\mu h\in V_\mu$. Here orthogonal means that $h-\Pi_\mu h$ has inner product zero with every vector in $V_\mu$. For each fixed $w\in\mathbb R^d$, put $v_w(s)=\sum_{j=1}^d\phi_j(s)w_j$ and $\delta_w=[T^\pi v_w-v_w]_\mu$. Then $\|\delta_w\|_\mu^2$ and $\|\Pi_\mu\delta_w\|_\mu^2$ are well-defined real numbers, including when some state weights vanish or the features are linearly dependent.
def-projected-bellman-error:
## Definition

Let $S$ be a nonempty finite state set of a finite Markov decision process, let $0\leq\gamma<1$, let $\pi$ be a stationary Markov policy, and let $\mu:S\to[0,1]$ satisfy $\sum_{s\in S}\mu(s)=1$. The function $\mu$ is a fixed state-weighting distribution; it need not be stationary for $\pi$. Let $d$ be a positive integer, let $\phi:S\to\mathbb R^d$ be a feature map, and for $w\in\mathbb R^d$ put $v_w(s)=\phi(s)^\mathsf T w$.

For real functions $f,g:S\to\mathbb R$, write $f\sim_\mu g$ when $\sum_{s\in S}\mu(s)(f(s)-g(s))^2=0$. Let $[f]_\mu$ denote the equivalence class of $f$ and define $\langle[f]_{\mu},[g]_{\mu}\rangle_\mu=\sum_{s\in S}\mu(s)f(s)g(s)$ and $\|[f]_\mu\|_\mu^2=\langle[f]_{\mu},[f]_{\mu}\rangle_\mu$. Let $H_\mu$ be the resulting finite-dimensional real inner-product space, and let $V_\mu$ be the span in $H_\mu$ of the equivalence classes of the $d$ coordinate feature functions.

For $h\in H_\mu$, let $\Pi_\mu h$ be the unique vector in $V_\mu$ whose difference from $h$ is orthogonal to every vector in $V_\mu$. The Bellman-error vector for $v_w$ is $\delta_w=[T^\pi v_w-v_w]_\mu$. Define the mean square Bellman error and mean square projected Bellman error by $\operatorname{BE}_\mu(w)=\|\delta_w\|_\mu^2$ and $\operatorname{PBE}_\mu(w)=\|\Pi_\mu\delta_w\|_\mu^2$.
thm-bairds-counterexample-off-policy-td-:
## Statement

Let the states be $S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_7\}$ and the two actions available at each state be $\mathrm{dashed}$ and $\mathrm{solid}$. All rewards are zero and $\gamma=0.99$. Under $\mathrm{dashed}$, the next state is each of $s_1,\ldots,s_6$ with probability $1/6$; under $\mathrm{solid}$, the next state is $s_7$ with probability $1$. The behavior policy has $b(\mathrm{dashed}\mid s)=6/7$ and $b(\mathrm{solid}\mid s)=1/7$ at every state, and the target policy selects $\mathrm{solid}$ with probability $1$. Use the uniform state weighting $\mu(s)=1/7$. For standard basis vectors $e_1,\ldots,e_8$ of $\mathbb R^8$, set $\phi(s_i)=2e_i+e_8$ for $1\leq i\leq6$ and $\phi(s_7)=e_7+2e_8$, and define $v_w(s)=\phi(s)^\mathsf T w$. For a behavior transition $(S,A,S')$, draw $S$ from $\mu$, draw $A$ from $b(\cdot\mid S)$, and draw $S'$ from the stated action transition law. Put $\rho=\pi(A\mid S)/b(A\mid S)$ and $\delta=\gamma v_w(S')-v_w(S)$, and define the expected semi-gradient TD(0) update by $\bar w^+=w+\alpha\,\mathbb E_{\mu,b}[\rho\delta\,\phi(S)]$. Also define the synchronous expected dynamic-programming update by $w^+=w+\frac{\alpha}{7}\sum_{s\in S}\big((T^\pi v_w)(s)-v_w(s)\big)\phi(s)$. For every step size $\alpha>0$, both deterministic update sequences starting at $w_0=(1,1,1,1,1,1,10,1)$ have Euclidean norm $\|w\|_2=(\sum_{i=1}^8w_i^2)^{1/2}$ tending to infinity. This is a claim about the stated expected/deterministic updates; it asserts no probability-one divergence result for individual stochastic TD trajectories.
thm-bellman-error-unlearnability-example:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice to form the infinite trajectory laws. Fix $0\leq\gamma<1$. An actionless finite Markov reward process (MRP) here means a nonempty finite state set with a joint probability law for next state and reward at each state. Consider the following two MRPs, each with its stated stationary state-weighting distribution, meaning that one transition leaves the distribution unchanged.

In MRP 1 the state set is $\{A,B\}$, with transitions $A\to B$ receiving reward $0$ deterministically and $B\to A$ receiving reward $1$ with probability $1/2$ or $B\to B$ receiving reward $-1$ with probability $1/2$. Its stationary weighting is $\mu_1(A)=1/3$, $\mu_1(B)=2/3$.

In MRP 2 the state set is $\{A,B,B'\}$, with transitions $A\to B$ and $A\to B'$ each receiving reward $0$ with probability $1/2$, $B\to A$ receiving reward $1$ deterministically, and $B'\to B$ or $B'\to B'$ each receiving reward $-1$ with probability $1/2$. Its stationary weighting is $\mu_2(A)=\mu_2(B)=\mu_2(B')=1/3$.

In both processes the observed feature is $\psi(A)=(1,0)$ and $\psi(B)=\psi(B')=(0,1)$, so a parameter $w=(a,b)^\mathsf T$ assigns values $v_w(A)=a$ and $v_w(B)=v_w(B')=b$. Starting from the stated stationary weighting, the two processes induce the same probability law on the observed feature/reward sequence $((\psi(S_n),R_{n+1}))_{n\geq0}$. Their mean square Bellman errors, defined as the stationary-weighted square of the conditional expected one-step TD error, are
$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{BE}_1(a,b)&=\frac13(\gamma b-a)^2+\frac23\left(\frac{\gamma}{2}(a+b)-b\right)^2,\\ \operatorname{BE}_2(a,b)&=\frac13\left((\gamma b-a)^2+(1+\gamma a-b)^2+(-1+(\gamma-1)b)^2\right).\end{aligned}
$$
MRP 1 has the unique minimizer $(a,b)=(0,0)$ and minimum $0$. With $D=1+\gamma+\gamma^2$, MRP 2 has the unique minimizer $(a,b)=\left(-\frac{\gamma}{D},\frac{\gamma}{2D}\right)$ and minimum $\frac{(\gamma+2)^2}{6D}$; also $\operatorname{BE}_2(0,0)=2/3$. For every $0<\gamma<1$ the minimizing parameters differ. Thus the Bellman-error objective and, for positive discount, its minimizing parameter are not determined by the observable feature/reward sequence law. An MRP here has no action-dependent policy; it is not an unseen-action offline-MDP policy-impossibility claim.
